claims: The Artemis II mission returned to Earth on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission had a safe splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
The crew of the Artemis II mission consisted of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The crew became the first humans to journey around the moon in over 50 years.
The Orion spacecraft entered Earth's atmosphere at approximately 25,000 mph (40,000 km/h).
The capsule hit the atmosphere at roughly 75 miles above the Pacific Ocean.
The capsule experienced temperatures around 5,000°F on its heat shield.
The USS John P. Murtha recovered the crew and capsule.
The Artemis II mission was a key test of the heat shield and crew systems for future moon landings.
Officials had some prior concerns regarding heat shield wear.
The re-entry and splashdown were successful.
The crew is now undergoing post-mission medical evaluations.
